contracts.commit_point: middleware.py line 80: result = handler(request) — the point where the agent tool call is actually executed; the blocked path returns the error ToolMessage at lines 74-78 before this statement, so a blocked call never commits.
contracts.declared_mechanism: secure_middleware(mode='enforce') builds Config/Interceptor and returns wrap_tool_call(_make_tool_call_handler(interceptor, session, ToolMessage)), registering the guard into LangChain v1's agent middleware tool-call dispatch (middleware.py:96-109). The _securevector callback serializes the tool-call args and calls Interceptor.evaluate_input, which in order: resolves permissions via resolve_permission (AppUnreachable -> Decision(True,'block','local app unreachable (fail-closed)') in enforce, allow in observe) at core.py:103-109; honors verdict.action=='block' as Decision(self.enforce,'block',...) at core.py:111-118; and runs secret/threat analysis via analyze, blocking only when enforce and risk_score >= cfg.threat_risk_threshold at core.py:127-137. Decision.blocked already accounts for mode and is only True when the call should actually be stopped (core.py:54-63, 17-20). When decision.blocked, _securevector returns tool_message_factory(content='[SecureVector] Tool ... blocked: ...', tool_call_id=call_id, status='error') WITHOUT calling handler (middleware.py:71-78); only otherwise does it reach handler(request) (middleware.py:80).
contracts.forbidden_condition: Control reaching the tool-execution statement handler(request) with Decision.blocked == True under enforce mode, where blocked is caused by any of: (a) LocalAppClient.resolve_permission returning verdict.action == 'block'; (b) a threat/secret finding on the serialized tool input with risk_score >= cfg.threat_risk_threshold; or (c) AppUnreachable during permission resolution (enforce is fail-closed, so an unreachable app yields blocked=True).
pending_binding_information: No runtime source in the supplied views constructs an agent with this middleware; the wiring middleware=[secure_middleware(mode='enforce')] in create_agent appears only in the module docstring example (middleware.py:10-16), so the concrete live agent registration is unconfirmed.

The semantics of LocalAppClient.resolve_permission verdicts and analyze risk scoring are outside the supplied views (core.py:104, 123).

contracts.protected_operation: Execution of an agent tool call through the wrap_tool_call handler path — the _securevector(request, handler) callback invoking handler(request) for the tool identified by request.tool_call['name'] with request.tool_call['args'].
contracts.protected_resource: Agent tools dispatched through the LangChain/LangGraph wrap_tool_call middleware on agents constructed with secure_middleware (tool calls carrying name, args, and id from the agent's ToolCallRequest).
contracts.protection_obligation: In enforce mode, a LangChain/LangGraph agent tool call must not execute when SecureVector's evaluation marks it blocked — i.e., when the local-app policy denies the tool id, when the tool input's secret/threat risk score is at or above the configured threat_risk_threshold, or when the local app is unreachable (fail-closed). The registered wrap_tool_call middleware must short-circuit such a call by returning an error ToolMessage instead of invoking the tool handler. (Merged from first- and second-phase reviewer opinions, which state the same obligation with overlapping citations.)
scope_limits: Blocking occurs only when cfg.mode == 'enforce'; the default 'observe' mode is fail-open and never blocks (core.py:17-20, 106-109, 118, 128; middleware.py:92-93).

Output-side scanning (scan_output) runs only after the tool has already executed and is log-only; it cannot retract a committed execution (core.py:148-157; middleware.py:81-83).
The mechanism requires the LangChain v1 middleware API (langchain.agents.middleware.wrap_tool_call) and raises ImportError otherwise (middleware.py:96-104).

Only tool calls routed through this middleware on agents constructed with it are gated; direct tool invocation outside the middleware and the CrewAI raising convenience path (guard_input, core.py:176-179) are outside this contract.

pending_binding_information: The lease is wired inline at each agent engine's turn-drive lifecycle boundary (AsyncExitStack entry in _drive_workspace; the leased() contextmanager) rather than via a registered hook callback; the agent-drives-to-guarded-effect dataflow is explicit in the cited lines, but whether the study's agent_lifecycle_hook category should cover inline drive-boundary wiring is a classification question.
contracts.protected_operation: Creating and driving the persistent sandbox session bound to a threaded workspace_key — session creation, credential materialization on the shared volume, and the turn drive (claude_code _drive_workspace -> _drive_session; langchain DeepAgentSession.leased -> acquire).
contracts.protected_resource: The durable agent workspace volume named by workspace_key (agent-namespaced per thread_id), serialized cross-worker by the Redis key 'agent:park:wslock:<workspace_key>'.
contracts.protection_obligation: No two workers may concurrently open or drive a sandbox session on the same durable agent workspace volume: both durable-workspace engines (claude_code and langchain_deep_agent) must hold the per-workspace Redis lease 'agent:park:wslock:<workspace_key>' across the whole threaded turn drive, acquired before any session is created, with a held lease a loud WorkspaceLeaseHeldError and release only via the token-checked compare-and-delete script.
scope_limits: Ephemeral uuid4 tool-face workspaces take no lease and never touch Redis (agent.py:410-412; session.py context at 128-129).
A crash frees the volume only after lease_ms expiry; there is no heartbeat (a heartbeated short lease expiring under a live drive is named as itself a corruption vector).
The guard is a Redis cross-worker mutex, deliberately not an in-container flock (lease.py:21-22).
DeepAgentSession.acquire's docstring notes a threaded run must reach it THROUGH leased; calling acquire directly on a threaded key bypasses the lease and is reserved for tests (session.py:147-150).

postgres_query's read-only enforcement is a separate SELECT/WITH prefix check routed through client.query (conn.fetch); it sits outside this approval gate, so a WITH-prefixed statement containing data modification would not traverse the gate.
Approval is a simple string match on the interrupt response and presumes a LangGraph runtime in which interrupt() suspends and resumes with a human reply (the tools re-raise GraphInterrupt).

contracts.commit_point: `self._now = target` immediately followed by `self._trace.append(self._now)` at working_dir.py lines 43-44, executed only after all three rejection branches have been passed.
contracts.declared_mechanism: Pre-commit validation inside WorkingDir.change_to_child_dir: (1) membership check `if target not in self._now.iterdir()` raising FileNotFoundError; (2) `if not target.is_dir()` raising NotADirectoryError; (3) `if target.is_symlink()` raising NotADirectoryError; the @tool wrapper catches any exception raised by these checks and returns a failure string, so the commit statements are reached only when all three checks pass.
contracts.forbidden_condition: Committing a working-directory change to a target that (a) is not found among the current directory's direct children (target not in self._now.iterdir() -> FileNotFoundError), (b) exists but is not a directory (not target.is_dir() -> NotADirectoryError), or (c) is a symlink (target.is_symlink() -> NotADirectoryError) — i.e., traversal or symlink-based escape beyond the current position, which the class docstring declares as preventing unauthorized (ultra vires) access to the file system outside the tool's permitted scope.
pending_binding_information: Implementation source for the static tools imported in file_system_cli/main.py lines 17-24 is not supplied; whether those file/process effects are bound to the WorkingDir position (which would create file- or process-stratum contracts) is unestablished.

The tool wrapper composes the agent-supplied string as `working_dir.where / target` (generate_dynamic_tools.py line 33); the supplied source does not document how target strings other than simple child names (e.g., values containing separators or nested segments) bind to the direct-child membership check — a behavior question left open, not decided here.

contracts.protected_resource: The WorkingDir instance's position state (self._now and the self._trace stack), scoped under the resolved root established in WorkingDir.__init__ (root.resolve()), which per the class docstring bounds the agent tools' capability range.
contracts.protection_obligation: Agent-initiated directory navigation via the change_to_child_dir agent tool (the LangChain @tool wrapper around WorkingDir.change_to_child_dir) must reject any target that is not a direct child of the current working directory, is not a real directory, or is a symbolic link, and must commit the new working-directory position (self._now = target) only after the direct-child membership, is_dir, and anti-symlink checks all pass. Ordinary CLI argument handling (argparse -r/--root) and the initial root existence check in WorkingDir.__init__ are entry/setup behavior, not part of this navigation obligation.

contracts.forbidden_condition: A command string matching any active dangerous-command rule (categories recursive_delete, force_kill, system_damage, shutdown) is assembled into full_command and reaches the subprocess.Popen spawn of the provider shell — i.e., ShellSession.execute proceeds past the check_command verdict on a match, or the guard is bypassed/disabled so that a matching destructive command is executed instead of being short-circuited with exit code 126.

contracts.protected_operation: Execution of a shell command through ShellSession.execute, which builds the provider command and spawns the shell subprocess; the operation is reached by the agent via the LangChain bash tool, which dispatches its agent-supplied command argument into session.execute.
contracts.protected_resource: The host OS shell/process execution environment reached through ShellSession.execute's subprocess spawn (the system shell and the machine state that destructive commands such as raw-disk writes, recursive deletion, forced kills, and shutdown target).
contracts.protection_obligation: Merged from both reviews (phase 1 German / phase 2 English, same obligation): destructive shell commands must not be assembled or executed by ShellSession.execute. check_command must scan the raw command string before any execution and block every match across the four evaluated categories — recursive deletion (rm with -r/-rf/-fr or --recursive, Remove-Item/ri -Recurse, rmdir|rd /s, del|erase /s), forced kills (kill/killall/pkill -9/-KILL/-SIGKILL, taskkill /f or /t, Stop-Process -Force), system damage (mkfs*, format <drive>:, dd of=/dev/ raw-disk writes, > /dev/sd|nvme|hd raw writes, fork bombs), and shutdown/reboot (shutdown, halt, poweroff, reboot, stop-computer, restart-computer, init 0|6, systemctl poweroff/reboot/halt) — honoring the global guard switch and disabled-category set, and returning ShellResult(exit_code=126) without spawning the shell subprocess.
scope_limits: The guard is opt-out by design: the master switch _guard_enabled (default True) and the per-category _disabled_categories set allow any rule to be bypassed; check_command returns GuardResult(blocked=False) when disabled or when the matched category is disabled (guard.py lines 30-36, 275-276, 288, 296-297).

Detection is a string/regex heuristic on the raw command string; only the enumerated bash/powershell/cmd patterns in _match_position and _CONTEXT_RULES are covered, and relative-path invocations of same-named binaries (e.g., ./reboot) are exempt from position-rule matching (guard.py lines 146-159, 281-284).

Blocked commands return ShellResult(exit_code=126) with a localized reason rather than raising; the guard is enforced only at the ShellSession.execute boundary shown, and no additional enforcement layer appears in the supplied views.
The guard scans only the raw command argument passed to ShellSession.execute; effects of other tools (write_file, edit, etc.) are outside this obligation.
Coverage of nested invocation (cmd /c ...) is asserted only for patterns appearing literally in the command string (guard.py lines 3-5).

Concurrency semantics of simultaneous audits for the same anomaly_id (read-modify-write race on bdh:session:{anomaly_id} with no locking in source) are unspecified and could weaken the five-rule guarantees.
contracts.protected_operation: Pre-flight audit decision (ALLOW/BLOCK with reason) for every LLM-proposed tool call, performed before the gateway's LangGraph Node 4 executes the tool.
contracts.protected_resource: The five-rule verdict path of audit_llm_tool_call exposed at POST /audit, backed by per-anomaly session state persisted at bdh:session:{anomaly_id}; the verdict gates execution of the four registered MCP tools (get_account_details, query_compliance_rules, block_account, escalate_to_investigator).
contracts.protection_obligation: The BDH watchdog's POST /audit pre-flight check must return BLOCK with a reason (never ALLOW) for any LLM-proposed tool call that violates any of the five deterministic audit rules — (1) context exhaustion: session tool_call_count exceeding 5 per anomaly; (2) hallucinated tool: tool_name absent from ALLOWED_TOOLS or args failing the tool's Pydantic schema; (3) state drift: tool_args.account_id differing from the session's target_account_id; (4) infinite loop: the identical call reaching repeat_count 3; (5) idempotency: a CRITICAL_TOOLS member (block_account, escalate_to_investigator) already recorded as executed for the anomaly — and must return ALLOW only when all five checks pass.
scope_limits: Verdict-only obligation: this contract covers the ALLOW/BLOCK decision returned by the BDH service; enforcement that the caller actually skips execution is a separate orchestrator-side contract.
State-drift (Rule 3) fires only when 'account_id' is present in tool_args (bdh_service/main.py:172), so escalate_to_investigator calls keyed on transaction_id are not drift-checked.

Rule 5 marks a critical tool as executed at audit-ALLOW time (bdh_service/main.py:201-202), not at the actual tool-effect commit, so the idempotency ledger tracks audited-allowed proposals rather than committed effects.
Session state expires after 300 seconds (bdh_service/main.py:125), bounding the context-exhaustion and idempotency windows per anomaly.
The /audit endpoint is unauthenticated with permissive CORS (bdh_service/main.py:315-320); agent mediation rests on the orchestrator dataflow, not on any authenticated caller binding.
Fail-open behavior lives caller-side (orcestrator/nodes.py:68-70); this contract does not govern callers that ignore or never obtain the verdict.
